excerpt: The tactics insurers use to deny or devalue an injury claim — recorded statements, biased exams, delay — and how to answer them.
keyTakeaways: Insurance companies use tactics including recorded statements, biased IMEs, unlimited medical record requests, pre-existing condition blame, delays, and lowball offers. Georgia's bad faith statute (O.C.G.A. § 33-4-6) imposes penalties up to 50% plus attorney fees. South Carolina's Act (S.C. Code § 38-59-20) provides similar protections. Never give a recorded statement or sign a blanket medical release without consulting an attorney.

faqs.question: Can I refuse to give a recorded statement?
faqs.answer: Yes. You are not legally required to give a recorded statement to the at-fault driver's insurer. Politely decline and direct them to your attorney.

faqs.question: Do I have to attend an independent medical exam?
faqs.answer: For pre-litigation claims, generally no. If a lawsuit is filed, a judge can order one under Georgia's O.C.G.A. § 9-11-35 or South Carolina's Rule 35. Your attorney can set conditions on the exam.

faqs.question: Can the insurer access all my medical records?
faqs.answer: Not without your consent. HIPAA protects your privacy. Never sign a blanket authorization. Your attorney provides only records relevant to your accident injuries.

faqs.question: What is a bad faith insurance denial?
faqs.answer: Bad faith occurs when an insurer unreasonably denies, delays, or undervalues a claim. Georgia's statute (O.C.G.A. § 33-4-6) allows penalties up to 50% plus attorney fees. South Carolina's Act (S.C. Code § 38-59-20) provides similar protections.

faqs.question: Should I accept the first settlement offer?
faqs.answer: Almost never. First offers are typically far below true value. Wait until you reach MMI and consult an attorney before accepting any offer.

faqs.question: How does hiring a lawyer change things?
faqs.answer: Significantly. Claimants with attorneys recover substantially more. Insurance companies know a lawyer will hold them accountable and take the case to trial if necessary. We handle cases on contingency — you pay nothing unless we win.
